title: When Apollo 13 Lost Oxygen in Deep Space
description: On April eleventh, 1970, Apollo thirteen launched toward the Moon, commanded by Jim Lovell, with Fred Haise and Jack Swigert. Two days in, at two hundred thousand miles from Earth, an oxygen tank exploded.

beats.text: Fifty-six hours into the mission, a routine oxygen tank stir triggered a massive explosion.
beats.visual: Apollo CSM and LM cutaway illustration showing service module layout, 1970

beats.text: Jack Swigert reported the emergency to ground control.
beats.visual: Apollo 13 Mission Control Houston operators at consoles, 1970

card.big: Houston, we've had a problem here.

beats.text: The sudden blast crippled electrical power and vented all oxygen from the service module.
beats.visual: photograph of the damaged Apollo 13 service module with missing panel, 1970

beats.text: The crew scrambled into the tiny lunar module, using it as a life-saving lifeboat.
beats.visual: Apollo 13 lunar module Aquarius in space against lunar background, 1970
queries: Apollo 13 lunar module Aquarius in space

beats.text: Engineers and astronauts created a duct-tape adapter called the mailbox to scrub lethal carbon dioxide.
beats.visual: photograph of the Apollo 13 improvised lithium hydroxide canister mailbox, 1970
queries: Apollo 13 mailbox lithium hydroxide canister NASA
